questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The surrounded opportunities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not the best living situation, with high prices, but a nice city and overall great culture

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Somewhat manageable. A lot of emails to keep account of, but it was fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much. Mostly just convenient contacts to ask any question one might have.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Some crucial questions was still unanswered before arrival. It would be nice to know these would be answered once arriving at the university.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There was a large variety to choose from, which the University provided. None of them are on the campus, but they are close by. Just check email account to take advantage of this.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is not a very big city. So most housing is fine in terms of distance to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was for from luxurious and nice. It was quite primitive, but it had all you needed for a very acceptable price.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit of shooting in the dark and not knowing whether you do something the correct way and when you are supposed to do some things. But it will always work out fine, it's just the uncertainty that is a bit annoying.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First digital registration to courses. Then there is a trial period of 2-3 weeks, where it is possible to try different courses. After that you're choosing the final courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Usual contact information on study advisors of the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesfull, could get more any course I wished for. Didn't seem like there was a problem with courses filling up.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont stress about it before arrival. Almost the entire final registration process happens during the first days.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not very economics oriented. More business and management oriented. But still some intersting courses that might not be offered at home.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Varies a lot across the courses. Some are very academic, some a not at all.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not enough group and seminar work in my opinion. It was mostly lectures and everything got recorded, so barely anyone showed up for the lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Marketing Management
International Trade
Introduction to Programming
Applied Econometrics
Introduction to Financial Accounting

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Programming - Great way of learning the basics of programming. Does not assume any academic background, can be useful for anyone.
International Trade - Great economics course, with a great professor. Bit difficult, but overall an intersting course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Residence Permit is a few hundred DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
All kinds of consumer products are very expensive everywhere. 

Public Transport within the city is free for students under 25. Outside the city it is very expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great sports opportunities, which all are very cheap or even free as well.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I mostly used the sports opportunities. But there are lots of social events as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely sports. Erasmus Network is also present in Geneva, despite not being a part of the program. They have tons of different social events that are not academic.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out into the mountains. They are the real attraction of Switzerland

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not a problem. Only language was sometimes difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the Erasmus events. They're filled with exchange students all looking for someone to hang out with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are a bit young in this university, but exchange students are more around the same age.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Not too different from rest of Europe.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Use student housing
Take advantage of sports opportunities
Go hiking in mountains.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check your email account frequently. Otherwise you might miss out on important stuff.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying to live in a completely different place.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to speaking english

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
